itinerary.title: Arusha to Tarangire National Park
body: After an early breakfast you are collected from your hotel and driven south-west to Tarangire National Park, about two to three hours on tarmac and a short stretch of park track. Tarangire is known for its large elephant herds, its ancient baobab trees and the permanent Tarangire River, which draws animals from across the region in the dry season.

After you enter the park you have a game drive through open woodland, swamps and river valleys, with a picnic lunch served at a scenic spot. Look for elephant, giraffe, zebra, wildebeest, impala and, with luck, lion and leopard, along with a wide range of birds. In the late afternoon you drive to your lodge for dinner and the night.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the park
meta.Accommodation: Kubu Kubu Tented Lodge or similar

itinerary.title: Tarangire to the Serengeti
body: After breakfast you leave early for the Serengeti. The route climbs through the Ngorongoro highlands and past the crater rim, then descends towards the Serengeti plains, with stops for viewpoints and a picnic lunch on the way.

You enter the Serengeti in the afternoon and begin a game drive across the central plains and kopjes. Lion, cheetah, elephant, giraffe and large herds of plains game are all possible, and your guide will choose the best areas for the season. You then drive to your camp for dinner and the night.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch

itinerary.title: Serengeti game drives
body: A full day in the Serengeti, with game drives in the best light at dawn and in the late afternoon. Your guide uses the season and recent sightings to decide where to go: river areas and kopjes for the big cats, open plains for herds and, in the right months, the migration.
Take a picnic lunch in the field or return to camp for a rest and enjoy a second drive, finishing with sundowners at camp or dinner under the stars.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the field

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater and return to Arusha
body: After an early breakfast you descend about 600 metres into the Ngorongoro Crater, the world's largest intact volcanic caldera. The crater floor holds a dense concentration of wildlife in a small area: lion, hyena, buffalo, wildebeest, zebra, hippo and flamingos on the soda lake, and with luck the rare black rhino.
You have a picnic lunch beside a hippo pool and spend the day on a game drive, then climb back to the rim in the afternoon.
From the rim you drive back to Arusha through the highlands, arriving in the early evening, where you are transferred to your hotel or the airport.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the crater

itinerary.title: Arrive in Arusha
body: You are met at Kilimanjaro International Airport (or at your Arusha hotel if you arrive by road) and transferred to your hotel in Arusha, about an hour from the airport. The rest of the day is free to rest after your journey.

In the evening your guide visits to brief you on the safari: the route, the timing of the early starts, what to pack for the park and how the days will run. This is the time to ask about dietary needs, photography interests and anything you would like to adjust.

meta.Activities: Airport transfer, Safari briefing

itinerary.title: Tarangire National Park
body: A full day of game drives in Tarangire, starting early when animals are most active. The guide follows the river and the swamps, where large elephant herds, buffalo and many bird species gather, and you can search for the cats that hunt along the ridges.
You have a picnic lunch in the park, a rest in the heat of the day and a second drive in the softer afternoon light.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the park
meta.Accommodation: Kubu Kubu Tented Lodge or similar

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara National Park
body: After breakfast you drive to Lake Manyara National Park, which sits at the foot of the Rift Valley escarpment. The park is compact and varied: groundwater forest with large troops of baboons and blue monkeys, open grassland with giraffe and buffalo, and the shallow lake, which attracts pelicans, flamingos and other waterbirds depending on the water level.
You spend the day on a game drive with a picnic lunch, then continue to your lodge near the escarpment for dinner and the night.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Birdwatching, Picnic lunch in the park
meta.Accommodation: Farm of Dreams Lodge or similar

itinerary.title: Ndutu and the southern plains
body: Game drives around Ndutu and the short-grass plains of the southern Serengeti ecosystem. Between roughly December and March, large herds of wildebeest and zebra gather here for calving, and the newborn animals draw lion, cheetah and hyena.
The guide follows the herds and predators through open plains, woodland and the shores of Lake Ndutu, with a picnic lunch in the field and an early evening return to camp.

body: You are met at Kilimanjaro International Airport (or at your Arusha hotel if you arrive by road) and transferred to your hotel in Arusha, about an hour from the airport. The rest of the day is free to rest after your journey.

In the evening your guide visits to brief you on the safari: the route, the timing of the early starts, what to pack for the park and how the days will run. This is the time to ask about dietary needs, photography interests and anything you would like to adjust.

itinerary.title: Tarangire National Park
body: A full day of game drives in Tarangire, starting early when animals are most active. The guide follows the river and the swamps, where large elephant herds, buffalo and many bird species gather, and you can search for the cats that hunt along the ridges.
You have a picnic lunch in the park, a rest in the heat of the day and a second drive in the softer afternoon light.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the park
meta.Accommodation: Kubu Kubu Tented Lodge or similar

itinerary.title: Lake Manyara National Park
body: After breakfast you drive to Lake Manyara National Park, which sits at the foot of the Rift Valley escarpment. The park is compact and varied: groundwater forest with large troops of baboons and blue monkeys, open grassland with giraffe and buffalo, and the shallow lake, which attracts pelicans, flamingos and other waterbirds depending on the water level.
You spend the day on a game drive with a picnic lunch, then continue to your lodge near the escarpment for dinner and the night.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Birdwatching, Picnic lunch in the park
meta.Accommodation: Farm of Dreams Lodge or similar

itinerary.title: Karatu to the Serengeti
body: After breakfast you leave early for the Serengeti. The route climbs through the Ngorongoro highlands and past the crater rim, then descends towards the Serengeti plains, with stops for viewpoints and a picnic lunch on the way.

You enter the Serengeti in the afternoon and begin a game drive across the central plains and kopjes. Lion, cheetah, elephant, giraffe and large herds of plains game are all possible, and your guide will choose the best areas for the season. You then drive to your camp for dinner and the night.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch

itinerary.title: Serengeti game drives
body: A full day in the Serengeti, with game drives in the best light at dawn and in the late afternoon. Your guide uses the season and recent sightings to decide where to go: river areas and kopjes for the big cats, open plains for herds and, in the right months, the migration.
Take a picnic lunch in the field or return to camp for a rest and enjoy a second drive, finishing with sundowners at camp or dinner under the stars.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the field

itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater and return to Arusha
body: After an early breakfast you descend about 600 metres into the Ngorongoro Crater, the world's largest intact volcanic caldera. The crater floor holds a dense concentration of wildlife in a small area: lion, hyena, buffalo, wildebeest, zebra, hippo and flamingos on the soda lake, and with luck the rare black rhino.
You have a picnic lunch beside a hippo pool and spend the day on a game drive, then climb back to the rim in the afternoon.
From the rim you drive back to Arusha through the highlands, arriving in the early evening, where you are transferred to your hotel or the airport.

meta.Activities: Game drive in a 4x4 with pop-up roof, Picnic lunch in the crater

itinerary.title: Fly to Zanzibar
body: After breakfast you transfer to the airport for a flight to Zanzibar. On arrival you are met and taken to your beach hotel on the island, and the rest of the day is yours to swim, walk on the beach and unwind after the safari.

itinerary.title: Stone Town and spice farm visit
body: A guided half day in Stone Town, the UNESCO-listed old quarter of narrow lanes, carved doors, markets and historic houses. You then visit a spice farm, where you can see and taste cloves, cinnamon, vanilla and other spices. The afternoon is free.

meta.Activities: Guided walking tour, Spice farm visit
meta.Accommodation: Beach hotel on Zanzibar (confirmed in your quote)

itinerary.title: Departure from Zanzibar
body: Enjoy a last swim and breakfast, then transfer to Zanzibar airport for your onward flight, depending on your flight time.

itinerary.title: Marangu Gate to Mandara Hut
body: After breakfast you are driven to Marangu Gate, where you register with the park and meet your guides and porters. You begin walking through lush montane rainforest, where blue and colobus monkeys can often be seen, up a well-graded path to Mandara Hut.
The walk takes about three to five hours. You arrive in time for tea, a hot meal and a briefing for the next day.

meta.Activities: Trekking

itinerary.title: Mandara Hut to Horombo Hut
body: A steady climb out of the forest and into heath and moorland, with open views of Mawenzi and later of the Kibo summit. You walk slowly and take regular breaks, since pacing yourself is the key to acclimatisation.
The day ends at Horombo Hut, with a hot meal and an early night.

meta.Activities: Trekking

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation day at Horombo
body: A rest day at altitude, with an optional guided walk towards Zebra Rocks. Climbing high during the day and sleeping lower helps your body adapt to the thinner air, and the extra day improves your chances of reaching the summit.

meta.Activities: Acclimatisation walk

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut to Kibo Hut
body: You cross the high-altitude desert of the saddle between Mawenzi and Kibo, an open and barren landscape with little vegetation. You reach Kibo Hut in the early afternoon and rest, eat early and prepare your clothes and headlamp for the summit attempt that starts around midnight.

meta.Activities: Trekking

itinerary.title: Summit day: Uhuru Peak and descent to Horombo
body: You set off around midnight for the steep climb over loose volcanic scree to Gilman's Point on the crater rim, then continue along the rim to Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, the highest point in Africa, ideally arriving around sunrise. After photographs at the summit you descend to Kibo Hut for a rest and then continue down to Horombo Hut for the night.
It is a long day of about 12 to 15 hours of walking, and your guides monitor you throughout.

meta.Elevation: 4,700 m to 5,895 m, descending to 3,720 m
meta.Activities: Summit climb

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut to Marangu Gate
body: You descend through moorland and forest to Marangu Gate, where you collect your summit certificate, say goodbye to the crew and are transferred back to your hotel in Moshi or Arusha.
